name: Ouroboros Energy Kinetic Bleed Capacitor
description:
The Kinetic Bleed Capacitor is a wearable energy harvesting and storage unit that converts ambient kinetic and thermal energy from its user's movement, environmental vibration, and body heat into usable electrical charge. It mounts as a rigid dorsal pack roughly the size of a hardback book, connected via a mesh of piezoelectric filaments woven into a load-bearing vest. Under normal activity — walking, climbing, operating machinery — it accumulates a slow trickle charge stored in a dense graphene supercapacitor array. Under high-exertion scenarios such as combat or sprinting, charge accumulation accelerates dramatically.

What distinguishes the KBC from competing portable power cells is its dual-mode discharge architecture. It can bleed stored energy slowly into connected devices — maintaining a hacking rig, powering a medical automaton, sustaining a signal relay — or it can dump its entire charge in a single directed burst through a contact interface, functioning as an improvised high-voltage discharge weapon or a breaching tool capable of frying electronic locks and sensor grids. This dual use makes it uniquely dangerous in the eyes of regulators, who classify it differently depending on jurisdiction.

The KBC is ubiquitous among couriers, scavengers, and off-grid operators who cannot rely on municipal charging infrastructure. In the deeper residential stacks of GLMZ, where power rationing is enforced by OUROBOROS ENERGY's own metering systems, the KBC is both a survival tool and a political statement — a way of reclaiming energy from the grid that extracts it from you. Corporate security teams have learned to scan for them at checkpoints, not because of the burst-discharge capability, but because operatives use them to power equipment that should be dead.
tactical_use: Operatives use the KBC to maintain power-hungry equipment — hacking rigs, drones, medical units — without relying on disposable cells that leave a procurement trail. The burst-discharge function is used to fry electronic door locks, disable proximity sensors, and in close-quarters situations, incapacitate unarmored targets through conductive contact. Couriers running dead zones use it to guarantee their comms and navigation stay live. It is also used to jump-start vehicles, power breaching charges, and keep cybernetic systems running when a user's internal power supply is compromised.
cultural_context: In the lower stacks, carrying a KBC is a marker of self-sufficiency and distrust of the grid. OUROBOROS ENERGY's tiered metering system means that residents who draw above their allotment face punitive rates or outright cutoffs — the KBC is a workaround that has become a cultural symbol of resistance. Graffiti in stack districts sometimes depicts a KBC with the OUROBOROS logo crossed out. In corporate circles, the device is viewed as low-status survival gear, but off-grid teams and black-site operators value it precisely because it generates no purchase signature from a charging point.
story_hooks: A KBC recovered from a dead courier contains a residual charge pattern that — when analyzed — encodes a message, suggesting the courier was using charge-bleed timing as a dead-drop signal method.

OUROBOROS ENERGY has quietly pushed legislation in two districts to reclassify the burst-discharge function as a prohibited weapon, effectively banning the device — the players are asked to transport a shipment before the ban takes effect.

A modified KBC is found at a crime scene with the burst-discharge circuit bypassed to deliver a continuous high-voltage output — it was used as an execution tool, and the modification requires specialized knowledge that points to a specific manufacturer's workshop.

The players' KBC malfunctions during a run in a Faraday-shielded facility, dumping its entire charge into a connected medical automaton and triggering an emergency in the middle of a stealth operation.
